values.text: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI

CHoRUS is a controlled-access, multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution critical care dataset assembled by the CHoRUS Network as one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded Bridge2AI consortium. It is built from retrospective clinical data contributed by 14 hospitals within a collaboration spanning 20 academic centers and more than 60 consortium members, and is intended to support machine learning that characterizes acute and critical care illness, predicts complications, and measures treatment response. The current released dataset covers 50,000 patient admissions from intensive care, pediatric intensive care, and neonatal intensive care settings, together with 23 Tb of waveform data; the anticipated final dataset covers 100,000 patient admissions across nine data modalities from the contributing hospitals. Structured electronic health record data and waveform telemetry are held in a cloud enclave under controlled access, while clinical notes remain stored locally at contributing sites and only tokens derived from them are available centrally. The CHoRUS leadership team named in the cohort 2 training webinar comprises Eric Rosenthal (Massachusetts General Hospital), Azra Bihorac, Yulia Strekalova and Parisa Rashidi (University of Florida), Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth Houston), and Manlik Kwong (Tufts University).

Structured electronic health record data are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model; imaging follows DICOM, waveform telemetry follows WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema, EEG follows EDF+ and Persyst, and tokenized clinical notes follow the OHNLP open source schema.

NIH RePORTER lists Rosenthal, Eric S. as principal investigator of award 1OT2OD032701-01 at Massachusetts General Hospital. The cohort 2 webinar additionally names a CHoRUS leadership team without designating those members as principal investigators; they are recorded in the dataset description rather than here.
NIH RePORTER records project number 1OT2OD032701-01 and application ID 10472824 under this core project number.
Awarded through the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program; the fiscal year 2022 award amount recorded by NIH RePORTER is 5,880,300 US dollars, with a project period of 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30.

To generate data for machine learning and artificial intelligence applications aimed at characterizing acute and critical care illness, predicting complications, and measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness.

To develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset whose methods promote privacy, accountability, and clinical benefit, and to provision a holdout test set accessible for external model validation to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models in acute and critical care.

To create ethically sourced datasets and tools around artificial intelligence and to establish best practices for AI in health, as one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded Bridge2AI consortium.

There is an urgent need for infrastructure to support artificial intelligence and machine learning in critical care, and developing high-resolution multicenter datasets is a critical first step toward actionable and trustworthy AI.
Clinical data arrive in heterogeneous source formats; unified standards are needed to harmonize multimodal electronic health record, waveform, imaging, and text data.

Data are collected retrospectively from 14 contributing hospitals drawn from a network of 20 academic centers and are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, with imaging from PACS in DICOM, bedside telemetry in WFDB, EEG in EDF+ and Persyst, and clinical notes extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit. The current released dataset described on chorus4ai.org comprises 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU and NICU, 1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data; the anticipated final dataset is 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities. All data types are controlled access. OMOP and telemetry data are worked with inside the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud enclave; clinical notes remain stored locally at contributing sites with only tokens available. The dataset is intended to support characterizing acute and critical care illness, predicting complications, and measuring treatment response, and the award abstract states that a holdout test set will be provisioned for external validation of models.

values.text: Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI

CHoRUS is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution, controlled-access critical care dataset produced by the Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI project, one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded Bridge2AI consortium. Data are collected retrospectively from the clinical systems of 14 data contributing hospitals within a collaboration spanning 20 academic centers, and are harmonized to unified standards: structured electronic health record data are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, imaging from PACS is held as DICOM, bedside monitor telemetry as WFDB waveforms, hospital EEG as EDF+ and Persyst, and clinical notes are extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit. The current released dataset reported by the project website comprises 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU and NICU settings, 1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data; the anticipated final dataset covers 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities. All data types are under controlled access. As presented in September 2025, OMOP and telemetry data reside in a cloud enclave, clinical notes are stored locally at the contributing sites except for tokens, imaging de-identification was in process for a larger cohort, and EEG extraction was in process.
Released to approved users under controlled access; data acquisition, standardization and modality expansion ongoing within the NIH project period 2022-09-01 through 2026-11-30.
The CHoRUS project website carries a site-wide banner reading "This repoitory is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives" (spelling as published).

The two mid-tier sources report different admission totals for the released data: the project website (project_documentation, higher ranked) states a Current Released Dataset of 50,000 patient admissions, while the September 2025 AIM-AHEAD informational webinar (cohort_2_webinar) states that "As of August 2025" the dataset "covers 14 different hospitals with over 45K unique admissions"; the higher-ranked website figure is used here and the webinar figure is recorded in this caveat. Imaging volume is likewise reported two ways and on different units: the website reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data, the webinar reports 1000 images currently available with de-identification in process for a larger cohort. Anticipated final figures (100,000 admissions, 9 modalities) are stated by the website as anticipated, not released. The webinar's data-type table has a Metadata column containing both "Yes" and "Planned" values, but the table's text is interleaved in the bundle in a way that does not permit reliable assignment of Yes/Planned to individual data types, so per-modality metadata status is not asserted here. The chorus-ai GitHub overview was captured 2025-11-14 and is the lowest-ranked source in the bundle.

CHoRUS is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution critical care dataset generated by the Bridge2AI CHoRUS data generation project, one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded Bridge2AI consortium, under NIH award OT2OD032701. Data are collected retrospectively from intensive care admissions at contributing hospitals and are held under controlled access in a cloud enclave. The project website reports a currently released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU and NICU settings, comprising 1.6 billion rows of OMOP-standardized electronic health record data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data; the anticipated final dataset is 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals, assembled by a consortium of more than 60 members across 20 institutions. Nine data modalities are documented - demographics, medication administration (time-stamped at each infusion change or dose administration), procedures, nursing flowsheets (high-frequency documentation), diagnoses, clinical notes (extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit), imaging from PACS, waveform telemetry from bedside monitors and gateway/middleware, and waveform EEG from hospital databases. Structured EHR data and telemetry sit in the shared enclave; clinical notes are stored locally at contributing sites with only tokens shared. The project also intends to sequester a holdout test set for external validation of models.
The project website carries a site-wide banner reading "This repoitory is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives."

Imaging coverage was partial at the August 2025 snapshot, with roughly 1,000 images available and de-identification in process for a larger cohort.
EEG data extraction was still in process as of August 2025, so EEG coverage of the released admissions was incomplete.
Clinical notes are stored locally at contributing sites and only tokens are available in the shared enclave, so analyses requiring full note text cannot be performed on the shared data.

Data come from 14 data contributing hospitals within a collaboration of 20 academic centers and cover acute and critical care admissions only, so the population is not a general hospital or general population sample.
The released dataset of 50,000 admissions is roughly half the anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions, and modality-level metadata publication was incomplete.
Analyses run on the current release may not generalize to the completed dataset, whose composition across modalities is expected to change.

Access to the dataset is controlled. Users of the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program must sign a licensing agreement included in the registration form before gaining access to the dataset, and a ".edu" email address is required to gain access; program administrators assist with this access where needed and the requirement is not a barrier to acceptance into the training program.

The chorus-ai GitHub organization states that its project is licensed under the MIT License, with individual repositories carrying MIT or Apache-2.0; this covers CHoRUS software and tooling rather than the clinical dataset.

The bundle states the licensing agreement requirement only in the context of the training program registration flow and does not reproduce the agreement or name a data use license for the dataset itself.

All modalities are under controlled access. Access requests are directed to named CHoRUS contacts (dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org). For the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program, participants complete a registration form giving name, email and institution and sign the licensing agreement included in that form; once access is granted and compute is provisioned, an email is sent to the participant. A ".edu" email address is required to gain access to the dataset.

The bundle names access contacts but does not name a data access committee, its membership, an access decision timeframe, or an appeal process. Massachusetts General Hospital is recorded as accountable organization because it is the awardee organization for OT2OD032701 and hosts the program manager; the bundle does not use the term data steward.

All nine documented data types are marked as controlled for access control, and access requires a signed licensing agreement and an institutional (".edu") email address. Data are worked with inside a cloud enclave rather than distributed as files.

The bundle does not state HIPAA, GDPR or export-control determinations for the dataset; HIPAA and GDPR compliance appear only as topics of a training workshop on IRB, data compliance and quality assurance.
OMOP Common Data Model relational tables

Demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets and diagnoses, held under controlled access in the cloud enclave, with published metadata against the OMOP schema (with extensions for nursing flowsheets).
Notes are extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit; note text remains stored locally at contributing sites and only tokens are shared. Metadata publication was planned as of August 2025.
Imaging obtained from PACS, under controlled access; metadata publication was planned as of August 2025.
Waveform telemetry from bedside monitors and gateway/middleware, documented against an extended PhysioNet schema.
Waveform EEG from hospital databases, documented against the open-source EDF+ and Persyst schemas; metadata publication was planned as of August 2025.

The dataset is made available beyond the contributing centers under controlled access: the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program expands access to CHoRUS data for up to 30 selected trainees per cohort, who work with the data on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud after signing the licensing agreement.
As of August 2025, the datasets are being used for training activities and publications.

The AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program (Cohort 2, running November 2025 to July 2026) has trainees use the data and tools on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud to create practical use cases and conduct research, presenting works-in-progress posters at the Bridge2AI and AIM-AHEAD 2026 annual meetings.
Characterization reports are produced from site submissions and returned to the contributing sites (CHoRUSReports).
Building machine learning and AI models to characterize acute and critical care illness
Predicting complications and deterioration in patients with acute or critical illness
The project's stated aim is to build ML- and AI-derived models that improve the care and outcomes of patients requiring critical care.
External validation of clinical AI models
Evaluating externally developed models against a sequestered holdout dataset
Intended to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care.
Hands-on trainee research on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud
Canonical Jupyter notebooks, OHDSI/OMOP common data model workshops and clinical deep learning exercises
The project cultivates expertise in the lay and scientific community to improve AI literacy and utilization through multimodal educational approaches.
Analyses incorporating social determinants of health and contextual factors, such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital, supported by geocoding of OMOP Location entities.
The sequestered holdout set is intended to support external validation and thereby aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care.

Because the data derive from critically ill patients, the project frames privacy, accountability and clinical benefit as conditions on future use, with patient-focused work determining the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health.
Community perspectives gathered through ethics focus groups determine what data is appropriate for public sharing, so the shareable scope of future releases depends on those findings.
Ciera McCrary, Program Manager, Massachusetts General Hospital, listed as the project contact on the CHoRUS website (cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu, address as printed on the site).
Access requests are handled by dbold@emory.edu and by Jared Houghtaling (jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org), listed as the contacts of the chorus-ai organization.

The chorus-ai GitHub organization maintains 28 repositories of CHoRUS software and documentation; versions, maintainers and other package metadata are tracked on a package status page, with contributor and user documentation compiled in the chorus-developer repository.

The released dataset is being expanded toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. As of August 2025, de-identification of a larger imaging cohort and extraction of EEG were in process, and metadata publication for clinical notes, imaging and EEG was planned.
The bundle does not state an update frequency or a versioning policy.

Contributing sites submit regular status updates on their extraction and curation progress, either through the GitHub interface directly or through a Google Form whose submissions update GitHub status and issue information automatically; these statuses feed the Standards Project and the Data Acquisition Project. Clinical collaborators contribute to semantic mapping through the chorus-mapping repository under a clinical validation SOP. Problems encountered in creating or submitting a data extract are posted in the Standards Discussions or Data Acquisition Discussions.
CHoRUS project website (https://chorus4ai.org/), with pages on the team, project overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset and learning resources.

chorus-ai GitHub organization (https://github.com/chorus-ai), 28 public repositories providing software and tooling for clinical data, validated semantic mappings, standard operating protocols for contributing sites, and project management overviews.
Chorus_SOP - centralized SOP documentation site with an interactive workflow diagram describing the step-by-step process for extracting and contributing clinical data to CHoRUS.
chorus-mapping - documentation and pooled tabular mappings with an associated clinical validation SOP for contributing to mapping efforts.
chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources - waveform documentation, conversion scripts, and resources supporting the preparation and release of waveforms.
chorus-extract-upload - tools to create and upload a CHoRUS Data Extract; chorus-container-apps - dockerized container applications and configurations deployed to support CHoRUS services on Azure.
privacy_scan_tool - a privacy scan tool for medical records; CTP-deid; UF-Geocoding - open source code to geocode OMOP Location entities via DeGauss.
CHoRUSReports - repository producing characterization reports returned to sites following their data submissions.
Bridge2AI project page for CHoRUS (www.bridge2ai.org/chorus) and the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care training program call for applications hosted on AIM-AHEAD.net.

Four sources were used, ranked: the CHoRUS project website (project_documentation, tier 2), the NIH RePORTER project page for OT2OD032701 (tier 4), the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Cohort 2 informational webinar of September 2025 (tier 4), and a 2025-11-14 capture of the chorus-ai GitHub organization overview (tier 5). The 2022 award abstract is written in the future tense about project plans and is recorded here as intention rather than as current dataset state. Volume figures differ between the tier-2 website (50,000 released admissions) and the tier-4 webinar (over 45K unique admissions as of August 2025); the higher-ranked figure is stated with the disagreement noted at the affected instance. The webinar's imaging figure (1,000 images) and the website's (7,642 admissions with radiology data) count different units and are both retained. The 23 Tb waveform figure is reported for waveform data only, so no dataset-wide size is recorded.

values.text: Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)
Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)
RO-Crate packaging with provenance graphs and rich metadata, produced using the FAIRSCAPE framework.

The June 2026 Data Release (Beta) of Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence (CM4AI), the Functional Genomics Grand Challenge of the NIH Bridge2AI program. CM4AI generates multi-modal data — protein-protein interaction, spatial protein localization, and genetic perturbation — in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (with or without paclitaxel or vorinostat) and in KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells (with or without differentiation). This release distributes ten ZIP archives through the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) and comprises: perturb-seq data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment and for undifferentiated (parental) KOLF2.1J iPSCs; SEC-MS data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment, undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs, and iPSC-derived neuron progenitor cells, neurons and cardiomyocytes; AP-MS data for treated MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells; and immunofluorescence images of MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment. Corresponding raw mass spectrometry and sequence data are deposited in external repositories. The release is explicitly interim: computed cell maps are not included, and some component datasets remain under temporary pre-publication embargo.

Clark T; Parker J; Al Manir S; Axelsson U; Ballllosero Navarro F; Chinn B; Churas CP; Dailamy A; Doctor Y; Fall J; Forget A; Gao J; Hansen JN; Hu M; Johannesson A; Khaliq H; Lee YH; Lenkiewicz J; Levinson MA; Marquez C; Metallo C; Muralidharan M; Nourreddine S; Niestroy J; Obernier K; Pan E; Polacco B; Pratt D; Qian G; Schaffer L; Sigaeva A; Thaker S; Zhang Y; Bélisle-Pipon JC; Brandt C; Chen JY; Ding Y; Fodeh S; Krogan N; Lundberg E; Mali P; Payne-Foster P; Ratcliffe S; Ravitsky V; Sali A; Schulz W; Ideker T, 2026, "Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)", https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, University of Virginia Dataverse, V2

Deposited to the University of Virginia Dataverse by Justin Niestroy, with a deposit date of 2025-02-27. The CM4AI project portal reports cumulative project-wide data holdings of 1,374 protein interactions, 53,788 immunofluorescent images, 7,023 total proteins investigated, 11,739 genes targeted and 21.4 TB of data volume; these are project-level totals across all CM4AI data streams and are not counts for this release alone. The CM4AI Dataverse collection carries the notice "This collection is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives."

The CM4AI project portal lists this release under the heading "June 2026 Data Release (Beta)" but gives "Released on: June 17, 2025"; the University of Virginia Dataverse record for the same DOI gives a Publication Date of 2026-06-17 and file publication dates of Jun 17, 2026. The Dataverse record is the higher-ranked source and its date is used here; the portal's 2025 date is recorded as a conflict. The Dataverse description block for this release ends with a trailing "(2025-06-30)" stamp identical to that on the June 2025 and October 2025 releases, indicating description text carried forward between releases. Three immunofluorescence image archives carry a file publication date of Jul 15, 2026, later than the 2026-06-17 publication date of version 2.0. Unlike the March 2025, June 2025 and October 2025 release pages, the June 2026 file listing carries no per-file descriptions, so modality and content detail for individual archives is drawn from the project preprint and from earlier release pages and is flagged as such where used.

To deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-Ready data, produced from multimodal interrogation of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric and cardiac disorders, in disease-relevant cell lines under perturbed and unperturbed conditions.

To produce ethical, AI-ready datasets of cell architecture, inferred from multimodal data collected for human cell lines, in order to enable transformative biomedical artificial intelligence research.

To map the spatiotemporal architecture of human cells and use these maps toward the grand challenge of interpretable genotype-phenotype learning, creating a library of large-scale maps of cellular structure and function across demographic and disease contexts.

In genomics and precision medicine, machine learning models are often "black boxes" that predict phenotypes from genotypes without revealing the mechanisms by which such translation occurs. This dataset is intended to supply the matched data and tools needed to build "visible" machine learning systems built directly on knowledge maps of cell and tissue architecture.

Existing biomedical datasets frequently lack the properties needed for reliable AI use. This project addresses that gap by defining and supplying AI-Ready data: FAIR data of known provenance, fully characterized and validated, with machine-readable provenance graphs of computations, data, software and models, explainable within stated limitations, and ethically obtained, licensed and distributed.
Interpretable genotype-phenotype learning, in which predictions are traced to multi-scale cell and tissue architecture rather than produced by an opaque model.
Development of "visible" machine learning systems, including visible neural networks built directly on knowledge maps of cell and tissue architecture.
AI-ready datasets to support research in functional genomics
Analysis of cell architectural changes and interactions in the presence of specific disease processes, treatment conditions, or genetic perturbations
These laboratory data are not to be used in clinical decision-making or in any context involving patient care without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval.

Nourreddine S, Doctor Y, Dailamy A, Forget A, Lee YH, Chinn B, Khaliq H, Polacco B, Muralidharan M, Pan E, Zhang Y, Sigaeva A, Hansen JN, Gao J, Parker JA, Obernier K, Clark T, Chen JY, Metallo C, Lundberg E, Ideker T, Krogan N, Mali P. A PERTURBATION CELL ATLAS OF HUMAN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS. bioRxiv. 2024 Nov 4; 2024.11.03.621734. PMCID PMC11580897. doi 10.1101/2024.11.03.621734
Listed by the release record as a related publication reporting analysis of the CRISPRi perturbation cell atlas of human induced pluripotent stem cells.
This is an interim release; the data are not yet in completed final form.
The release does not contain predicted cell maps, which will be added in future releases.
Some component datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo. The perturb-seq data for KOLF2.1J iPSCs and for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells are listed in the external data links as embargoed.
The protein-protein interaction (SEC-MS), protein localization (IF imaging) and CRISPRi perturb-seq data interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap.
The current release is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets rather than for integrated cross-modality analysis.
Data in this release were derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large.

All modalities in the release, which derive from two cell lines: MDA-MB-468, a triple negative breast cancer line established from a metastatic pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma, and KOLF2.1J, an iPSC line derived from a healthy male Northern European donor.
Immunofluorescence confocal microscopy image showing the subcellular localization of a protein of interest in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells, untreated or treated with paclitaxel or vorinostat
Size-exclusion chromatography mass spectrometry protein elution profile for a proteome-wide protein complex and interaction measurement
Affinity purification mass spectrometry protein-protein interaction measurement in treated MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells
Single-cell CRISPRi perturbation transcriptional profile mapping transcriptional and fitness phenotypes associated with a targeted gene
Raw single-cell sequence read set underlying the CRISPRi perturbation screen

Primary experimental measurement on cultured human cell lines: affinity purification mass spectrometry and size-exclusion chromatography mass spectrometry for protein-protein interactions, immunofluorescence confocal microscopy for spatial protein localization, and single-cell CRISPR perturbation screens for transcriptional and fitness phenotypes.

Derived processing of primary measurement: the KOLF2.1J perturbation cell atlas archive is distributed alongside a separate archive of the underlying raw sequence data, indicating that the atlas is a processed product of that raw data.
Inferred from the paired archive names cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip and cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_raw_sra.zip; the June 2026 release listing carries no per-file processing description.

Data were not collected from individuals. All measurements were made on established human cell lines obtained from third-party repositories: MDA-MB-468 from ATCC and KOLF2.1J from the Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Initiative (HipSci) resource.
Affinity purification mass spectrometry (AP-MS) performed on endogenously tagged cell lines, for protein-protein interaction mapping.
Size-exclusion chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (SEC-MS), for proteome-wide protein complex and interaction mapping.

Immunofluorescence-based staining and confocal microscopy (ICC-IF) for spatial proteomics, using the Human Protein Atlas resource of antibodies, with automated fixation and permeabilization protocols established for the MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 cell lines.
Single-cell CRISPR interference perturbation screens, performed using the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit, with a CRISPR lentiviral library and cell lines expressing inducible dCas9.

University of California San Francisco: mass spectrometry based protein-protein interaction data. The project preprint identifies the Krogan Laboratory as the source of the PPI networks entering the CM4AI pipeline.
Mass spectrometry protein-protein interaction data generation

The June 2026 release lists production locations collectively without assigning modalities; the laboratory attribution is drawn from the CM4AI project preprint and from per-file descriptions on earlier release pages.
Stanford University: immunofluorescence spatial proteomics imaging. The project preprint identifies the Lundberg Laboratory as the source of the IF images entering the CM4AI pipeline.

The June 2026 release lists production locations collectively without assigning modalities; the laboratory attribution is drawn from the CM4AI project preprint and from per-file descriptions on earlier release pages.
University of California San Diego: genetic perturbation mapping by single-cell CRISPR screening, and multimodal data integration.
Genetic perturbation screening and data integration

Modality attribution inferred from the project preprint's account of the genetic perturbation mapping work; the June 2026 release lists University of California San Diego among four production locations without assigning modalities.
University of Virginia: AI-readiness packaging, metadata, provenance graphs and archival deposit of the release.

The release record gives a data creation date of 2025-02-27 and a deposit date of 2025-02-27. The funding award supporting data generation runs from 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31 per NIH RePORTER, and the release record states that the dataset will continue to be updated through the end of the project in November 2026. No explicit start and end dates for data collection are stated.

Targeted selection of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes implicated in cancer, neuropsychiatric and cardiac disorders, interrogated in disease-relevant cell lines under perturbed and unperturbed conditions. Perturb-seq of 200 genes in the triple-negative breast cancer cell line and immunofluorescence imaging of 523 proteins, per the CM4AI project portal's description of the flagship breast cancer dataset.
Expressed genome-scale CRISPRi perturbation in undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs, covering 11,739 targeted genes rather than a sampled subset.
The project portal describes the iPSC perturb-seq component as covering more than 11,000 genes at whole-genome scale and reports 11,739 genes targeted as a project-level figure.

MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419), a triple negative breast cancer cell line established from a metastatic site pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with a metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma. The line has been extensively used to study triple-negative breast cancer and is well characterized, with transcriptomic, mutational profile and whole-genome sequencing data available.
KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3), an induced pluripotent stem cell line derived from a healthy male Northern European donor.
Human induced pluripotent stem cell line
Available from the Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Initiative (HipSci) resource, and available for access by not-for-profit organizations via a simple MTA.
Raw size-exclusion chromatography mass spectrometry data for KOLF2.1J iPSCs (undifferentiated, NPC, neuron and cardiomyocyte), deposited in the MassIVE repository and linked from the release record.
Raw size-exclusion chromatography mass spectrometry data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment, deposited in the MassIVE repository and linked from the release record.
Raw affinity purification mass spectrometry data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells treated with paclitaxel, deposited in the MassIVE repository and linked from the release record.
Raw affinity purification mass spectrometry data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells treated with vorinostat, deposited in the MassIVE repository and linked from the release record.
Raw sequence data underlying the KOLF2.1J CRISPRi perturbation screen, distributed in the release as cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_raw_sra.zip.
Perturb-seq data are distributed both as a processed CRISPRi perturbation cell atlas and as the underlying raw sequence data, in separate archives.

Inferred from archive naming in the June 2026 file listing; that listing carries no per-file processing description. Computed cell maps, which the project produces by self-supervised multimodal embedding and multi-resolution community detection, are explicitly not included in this release.

Clark T, Parker J, Schaffer L, Obernier K, Al Manir S, Churas CP, Dailamy A, Doctor Y, Forget A, Hansen JN, Hu M, Lenkiewicz J, Levinson MA, Marquez C, Nourreddine S, Niestroy J, Pratt D, Qian G, Thaker S, Bélisle-Pipon JC, Brandt C, Chen J, Ding Y, Fodeh S, Krogan N, Lundberg E, Mali P, Payne-Foster P, Ratcliffe S, Ravitsky V, Sali A, Schulz W, Ideker T. Related publication cited by the release record as the reference for this dataset.
Project portal providing documentation, data release listings, tools and publications for CM4AI.
CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas of iPSCs, hosted on Figshare
External data link given in the release record.
Cell Mapping Toolkit / CM4AI data integration pipeline software, released under a BSD-3 open source license via GitHub, with production-ready tools archived in Zenodo
Software used to integrate CM4AI input data streams; links to these tools are packaged in RO-Crates as part of CM4AI provenance representations.
Framework used to package CM4AI data, software, metadata and provenance graphs; released under an open source MIT License.
Two ZIP archives of affinity purification mass spectrometry data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells treated with paclitaxel (113.3 KB) or vorinostat (135.8 KB).
Three ZIP archives of immunofluorescence images of MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells: untreated (4.6 GB), paclitaxel-treated (3.8 GB) and vorinostat-treated (4.2 GB).

The October 2025 release described same-named archives as showing the spatial localization of 464 proteins of interest, imaged by immunofluorescence-based staining (ICC-IF) and confocal microscopy in the Lundberg Lab at Stanford University, with nuclei stained by DAPI, endoplasmic reticulum by a calreticulin antibody, microtubules by a tubulin antibody, and the protein of interest by a fourth antibody. The June 2026 archives carry different MD5 checksums from the October 2025 archives of the same names and no descriptions of their own, so the protein count and staining detail are not asserted here for this release.
Two ZIP archives of SEC-MS data: KOLF2.1J iPSCs and derivatives (171.8 KB) and MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment (93.9 KB).
KOLF2.1J CRISPRi perturbation cell atlas archive
One ZIP archive (30.2 KB) of the processed CRISPRi perturbation cell atlas for KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells.
One ZIP archive (73.3 KB) of raw sequence data for the KOLF2.1J CRISPRi perturbation screen.
One ZIP archive (1.1 MB) of release metadata.

All ten files are distributed as ZIP archives through the University of Virginia Dataverse. The dataset as a whole is too large to download as a single ZIP; individual files below the 1.9 GB web download limit may be selected from the files table, and the Dataverse Data Access API provides programmatic access. MD5 checksums are published for each archive.
2026-06-17 (version 2.0 published; seven of the ten archives published on this date)

Corresponding raw data are deposited outside the University of Virginia Dataverse: raw mass spectrometry data for the SEC-MS and AP-MS components in the MassIVE repository, and the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas of iPSCs on Figshare. The release record links to these external resources.

Some component datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo. The external data links for perturb-seq data in KOLF2.1J iPSCs and for perturb-seq data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells are both marked embargoed rather than pointing to an open repository.

The release record states that the dataset does not involve human subjects, that samples are de-identified, and that the data are not FDA regulated. The project preprint states that CM4AI data are non-clinical, deriving from tissue cultures.

The release record answers "De-identified Samples: Yes". The project preprint states that CM4AI data are non-clinical, from tissue cultures, and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.
The release record states "Human Subjects: No" and "FDA Regulated: No".
Ethical review for the release is handled by named CM4AI ethics contacts rather than by a named institutional review board; no IRB or ethics committee is identified in the release record.
Named ethical review contact for the release, per the Data Governance and Ethics section of the release record.

The release record names "Vardit Ravitsky (ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org)" as an ethical review contact and separately lists an author "Ravitsky V" with the ORCID 0000-0002-7080-8801 and an affiliation of University of Montreal. The two are treated as the same individual on the basis of matching surname and given-name initial; note that the stated affiliation (University of Montreal) and the email domain (thehastingscenter.org) differ.
Named ethical review contact for the release, per the Data Governance and Ethics section of the release record.

The project preprint states that a Data Access Committee will supervise ethical matters related to dataset distribution and potential dual licensing for commercial use; that is stated there as a planned arrangement. All ten archives in this release are listed with public file access.

The release record names "Jillian Parker (jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu)" as the Data Governance Committee contact and separately lists an author "Parker J" at the University of California, San Diego with the ORCID 0000-0003-4535-3486; the two are treated as the same individual on the basis of matching surname, given-name initial and institution.

values.text: Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)

The June 2026 Data Release of CM4AI (Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence), the Functional Genomics Grand Challenge in the NIH Bridge2AI program. CM4AI generates multi-modal data including protein-protein interaction (PPI), spatial localization, and genetic perturbation data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (with and without paclitaxel or vorinostat treatment) and induced pluripotent stem cells (with and without differentiation). This Beta release includes: Perturb-seq data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment and for undifferentiated (parental) KOLF2.1J iPSCs; SEC-MS data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment, undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs, and iPSC-derived neuron progenitor cells (NPCs), neurons, and cardiomyocytes; AP-MS data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with treatment; and immunofluorescence images in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment. CM4AI output data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework.

total_file_count and total_size_bytes are this record's own computation, not figures any source reports. They are the count and the sum of the ten files the June 2026 release listing enumerates with individual sizes: 113.3 KB, 135.8 KB, 3.8 GB, 4.6 GB, 4.2 GB, 171.8 KB, 93.9 KB, 30.2 KB, 73.3 KB and 1.1 MB, converted at 1 GB = 1e9 bytes and 1 KB = 1e3 bytes as the listing's rounded figures permit; the sum is therefore approximate to the precision of those rounded per-file figures. The project web portal separately states a "Data volume" of 21.4 TB for CM4AI as a whole, which is a figure about the project rather than about this release and disagrees with the derived release total by roughly three orders of magnitude; both are recorded and neither has been adjusted. Sources also disagree on the count of proteins imaged by immunofluorescence in MDA-MB-468: the March 2025 release states 563 proteins of interest per condition while the June 2025 and June 2026 releases state 464; the higher-ranked June 2026 release value (464) is used, and the March 2025 figure is recorded here as the superseded reading. The bundle does not state whether the two figures reflect a re-count, a filtering step, or a change in what is counted. Sources also disagree on the number of authors and the affiliation of one author: Sali A is affiliated to the University of California San Francisco in the bioRxiv preprint and to the University of California San Diego in the Dataverse release citations; the Dataverse releases are the higher-ranked source for this record and their attribution is used in creators. The bundle gives no ORCID for several named creators and no ROR or other registry identifier for any organization, so none is supplied.

To deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-Ready data, produced from multimodal interrogation of proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders in disease-relevant cell lines under perturbed and unperturbed conditions.
To map the spatiotemporal architecture of human cells and use these maps toward the grand challenge of interpretable genotype-phenotype learning.
To produce ethical, AI-ready datasets of cell architecture, inferred from multimodal data collected for human cell lines, to enable transformative biomedical AI research.

To broadly stimulate research and development in "visible" machine learning systems informed by multi-scale cell and tissue architecture, which are built directly on knowledge maps of cell and tissue architecture rather than being difficult-to-interpret black boxes.

In genomics and precision medicine, machine learning models are often "black boxes," predicting phenotypes from genotypes without understanding the mechanisms by which such translation occurs. This project addresses that deficiency by generating matched data and tools that enable creation of "visible" ML systems.

Much of cell structure remains uncharted; cell mapping technologies have typically been applied separately, and integration of multiple complementary data modalities provides the opportunity to incorporate biological structure robustly across physical scales.
AI model training on functional genomics data.
Analysis of cell architectural changes and interactions in the presence of specific disease processes, treatment conditions, or genetic perturbations.
Construction of hierarchical cell maps from fusion of protein interaction and imaging data, via self-supervised embedding followed by multi-resolution community detection.
AI-ready data for functional genomics research
AI-ready datasets to support research in functional genomics.
The release is intended as training data for AI models.
Analysis of cellular processes from the multi-modal measurements.
Study of cell architectural changes and interactions in presence of specific disease processes, treatment conditions, or genetic perturbations.
These laboratory data are not to be used in clinical decision-making or in any context involving patient care without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval.

The release does not contain predicted cell maps and is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets; use of it as a source of computed cell maps is not supported at this release.

This is an interim release. It does not contain predicted cell maps, which will be added in future releases. The current release is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets.
Analysis requires domain expertise to be meaningful.
Protein-protein interaction (SEC-MS), protein localization (IF imaging), and CRISPRi perturb-seq data interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap.
The data are not yet in completed final form; some datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo, and computed cell maps are not included in this release.
Data in this release was derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large.
Affinity purification-mass spectrometry data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells under paclitaxel and vorinostat treatment, distributed as two ZIP archives.

Spatial localization of 464 proteins of interest in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells, untreated and treated with paclitaxel or vorinostat, imaged by immunofluorescence-based staining (ICC-IF) and confocal microscopy in the Lundberg Lab at Stanford University. Nuclei were stained with DAPI (blue channel); endoplasmic reticulum with a calreticulin antibody (yellow channel); microtubules with tubulin antibody (red channel); and antibody against protein of interest (green channel).

Size exclusion chromatography-mass spectrometry data for KOLF2.1J iPSCs and derivatives and for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment, generated in the Nevan Krogan laboratory at the University of California San Francisco.
Genome-scale CRISPRi perturbation cell atlas and raw sequence data for KOLF2.1J human induced pluripotent stem cells.
Release metadata archive accompanying the June 2026 data release.
Immunofluorescence confocal image of MDA-MB-468 cells

Data generated in the MDA-MB-468 triple negative breast cancer cell line under three conditions: untreated, paclitaxel-treated, and vorinostat-treated. Includes perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS (treated conditions) and immunofluorescence imaging.
KOLF2.1J iPSC and derivative cell data

Data generated in undifferentiated (parental) KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells and in iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells, neurons, and cardiomyocytes. Includes perturb-seq (undifferentiated) and SEC-MS (all four cell states).

Subpopulations in this dataset are cell lines and differentiation states rather than human demographic groups: MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (untreated, paclitaxel, vorinostat) and KOLF2.1J iPSCs (undifferentiated, neural progenitor cells, neurons, cardiomyocytes).

Coverage differs by modality: perturb-seq covers MDA-MB-468 under treatment conditions and undifferentiated KOLF2.1J; SEC-MS covers MDA-MB-468 under treatment conditions and all four iPSC states; AP-MS covers MDA-MB-468 under treatment only; IF imaging covers MDA-MB-468 only.
Protein-protein interactions acquired by affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) on endogenously tagged cell lines.
Protein-protein interactions and complexes acquired proteome-wide by size-exclusion chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (SEC-MS).
Spatial subcellular protein localization acquired by immunofluorescence-based staining (ICC-IF) using Human Protein Atlas antibodies and high-resolution confocal microscopy.
Transcriptional and fitness phenotypes acquired by single-cell CRISPRi perturbation screens (perturb-seq).
Automated fixation and permeabilization protocols on a pipetting robot were established for MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 cell lines for spatial proteomics mapping.
A CRISPR lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors with 6 guide RNAs per gene was designed, and MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 CRISPR lines expressing inducible dCas9 were generated and characterized.
Single-cell CRISPR screens were performed using the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit.
Immunofluorescence imaging and spatial proteomics generated in the Lundberg Lab at Stanford University.
Size exclusion chromatography-mass spectrometry and affinity purification-mass spectrometry generated in the Nevan Krogan laboratory at the University of California San Francisco.

Data were generated from commercially available and repository-sourced human cell lines, not collected directly from human subjects. MDA-MB-468 is available from ATCC; KOLF2.1J is available from the Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Initiative (HipSci) resource to non-for-profit organizations via a simple MTA.
MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419), a triple negative breast cancer cell line established from a metastatic site pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with a metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma.
KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3) induced pluripotent stem cell line, derived from a healthy male Northern European donor.
Available from the Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Initiative (HipSci) resource; accessible by non-for-profit organizations via a simple MTA.
Downloaded PPI networks are processed using the node2vec deep learning model to reduce dimensionality, producing a PPI embedding that contains information about the protein's interactions.
IF images are processed using a Human Protein Atlas deep learning model to reduce dimensionality, producing an image embedding that contains information about protein localization.

The PPI and image embeddings are integrated to obtain a co-embedding for each protein using contrastive deep learning, learning co-embeddings such that the original embeddings can be reconstructed with minimal information loss and proteins with similar PPI and image embeddings have similar co-embeddings.
Community detection is performed based on the all-by-all similarities of pairs of proteins in the co-embedding space; the resulting hierarchy of protein communities is output as the final cell map.

Cell maps are annotated in a two-pronged approach: alignment to known protein function and pathway resources including the Gene Ontology (GO) and Reactome to determine protein assemblies with high overlap with known cell biology; and annotation using a large language model approach developed to name sets of proteins and assign a name confidence score.
Hierarchy evaluation stage of the MuSIC pipeline (cellmaps_hierarchyeval), which annotates the cell map with known resources such as GO.
DenseNet-121 / Human Protein Atlas image model

node2vec is used to embed protein-protein interaction neighborhoods; a Human Protein Atlas deep learning model is used to embed immunofluorescence images; a large language model approach is used to name sets of proteins and assign a name confidence score.

All ten files in the June 2026 release are distributed as ZIP archives via the University of Virginia Dataverse. Individual file download is available; the dataset as a whole exceeds the repository's 1.9 GB ZIP download limit, and the Data Access API is offered for programmatic access.

June 2026 release published 2026-06-17; the three immunofluorescence image archives in this release were published 2026-07-15. Earlier CM4AI releases: May 2024, March 2025 (published 2025-03-03), June 2025 (published 2025-07-01), October 2025 (published 2025-10-31).

Component datasets are additionally deposited in external repositories: SEC-MS data for KOLF2.1J iPSCs and for MDA-MB-468 in the MassIVE Repository; AP-MS data for MDA-MB-468 treated with paclitaxel and with vorinostat in the MassIVE Repository; the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas of iPSCs on Figshare. Perturb-seq data in KOLF2.1J iPSCs and in MDA-MB-468 are listed as embargoed.
CM4AI project web portal, https://cm4ai.org/, providing project documentation, data release listings, tools and training material.

MassIVE Repository deposits for SEC-MS data (KOLF2.1J iPSCs and derivatives; MDA-MB-468 with and without treatment) and for AP-MS data (MDA-MB-468 treated with paclitaxel; MDA-MB-468 treated with vorinostat).
Figshare deposit of the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas of iPSCs.
FAIRSCAPE AI-readiness framework, described with tutorial and installation instructions at https://fairscape.github.io, available under the MIT License.
Cell Mapping Toolkit (MuSIC pipeline), https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, with user documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/.
Open source Integrative Modeling Platform (IMP) package, http://integrativemodeling.org.
Network Data Exchange (NDEx), https://ndexbio.org, used to share cell maps.
CM4AI October 2025 Data Release (Beta), University of Virginia Dataverse, version 2.1. That release contained perturb-seq, SEC-MS and IF image data but no AP-MS data.

CM4AI June 2025 Data Release (Beta), University of Virginia Dataverse, version 2.1, published 2025-07-01. That revision added RGB immunofluorescent images, corrected RO-Crate metadata, and changed naming conventions.

CM4AI March 2025 Data Release (Beta), University of Virginia Dataverse, version 1.4, published 2025-03-03. That release included perturb-seq in undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs, SEC-MS in iPSCs and derivatives, and IF images stated there as covering 563 proteins of interest per condition.
Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - Data Release, University of Virginia Dataverse, V1, the May 2024 release cited in the CM4AI preprint.

Clark T et al., "Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence: AI-Ready Maps of Human Cell Architecture from Disease-Relevant Cell Lines", bioRxiv preprint describing the CM4AI project, its goals, methods, standards, datasets, software tools, status and future directions.
Nourreddine S et al., "A Perturbation Cell Atlas of Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells", bioRxiv 2024, PMCID PMC11580897, cited as a related publication for the perturb-seq component.

Schaffer LV, Hu M, Qian G et al., "Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics", Nature 642:222-231 (2025). Describes a U2OS multimodal cell map produced with the same AP-MS plus immunofluorescence integration approach and the Cell Mapping Toolkit; acknowledges Bridge2AI Program funding OT2 OD032742. Its data are a separate dataset from this release.

The Dataverse release records Human Subjects: No; De-identified Samples: Yes; FDA Regulated: No. The preprint states CM4AI data are non-clinical (from tissue cultures) and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.
Samples are recorded as de-identified. Data were derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines; the underlying cell lines are described as ethically sourced.
Ethical review for the project is held by the named ethics leads, who supervise ethical matters relating to dataset preparation, licensing, dissemination and Data Access.

The Ethics module works with the Data Acquisition, Tools, and Standards modules on ethical preparation, licensing, dissemination and Data Access supervision of CM4AI datasets, balancing openness of the data produced with protection of intellectual property and supervision and monitoring of potential efforts at commercialization.

CM4AI is organized into three pillars (Data, People, and Ethics) across six modules: Data Acquisition, Tools, and Standards; Skills and Workforce Development, and Teaming; and Ethics. Cell maps are hierarchical directed acyclic graphs in which each node represents an assembly of proteins in proximity at a given scale, spanning from large assemblies representing cell compartments to small assemblies of proteins in close proximity. The CM4AI project is a collaboration of UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, UVA, Yale, UT Austin, UA Birmingham, Simon Fraser University, and the Hastings Center. The University of Virginia Dataverse collection carries the notice that it is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives.

values.text: Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)

The June 2026 Data Release of Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence (CM4AI), the Functional Genomics Grand Challenge in the NIH Bridge2AI program. CM4AI generates multi-modal data including protein-protein interaction (PPI), spatial localization, and genetic perturbation data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (with and without paclitaxel or vorinostat treatment) and induced pluripotent stem cells (with and without differentiation). This Beta release includes perturb-seq data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment and undifferentiated (parental) KOLF2.1J iPSCs; SEC-MS data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment, undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs, and iPSC-derived neuron progenitor cells (NPCs), neurons, and cardiomyocytes; AP-MS data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with treatment; and immunofluorescence images in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment. The overarching objective of CM4AI is to deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data, produced from multimodal interrogation of chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes, and other proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders in disease-relevant cell lines under treated and untreated conditions.

Values are taken from the June 2026 Dataverse release (doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C), which the declared source ranking places at tier 1 and marks as superseding the October 2025 release. Where earlier Dataverse releases (March 2025, June 2025, October 2025) state different contents, those are facts about those earlier versions and are recorded under related_datasets rather than in this record's own slots. The CM4AI project web pages (tier 2) report cumulative project-level counts (1,374 protein interactions; 53,788 immunofluorescent images; 7,023 total proteins investigated; 11,739 genes targeted; 21.4 TB data volume) that are attributed to the CM4AI project as a whole rather than to this single release, and are therefore not asserted as release-level totals here. The bundle contains a Nature publication (tier 3) describing a U2OS cell map produced by the same investigators and pipeline; that is a distinct dataset and is recorded under related_datasets. The June 2026 release page carries a Dataset Description block dated (2025-06-30) although the release itself was published 2026-06-17; the release page also gives a Data Creation Date of 2025-02-27, which is reused verbatim from earlier releases in this Dataverse collection.

To map the spatiotemporal architecture of human cells and use these maps toward the grand challenge of interpretable genotype-phenotype learning.

To deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data, produced from multimodal interrogation of chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes, and other proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders in disease-relevant cell lines under treated and untreated conditions.
To produce ethical, AI-ready datasets of cell architecture, inferred from multimodal data collected for human cell lines, in order to enable transformative biomedical AI research.

To broadly stimulate research and development in "visible" machine learning systems informed by multi-scale cell and tissue architecture, which are not black boxes but are built directly on knowledge maps of cell and tissue architecture.

In genomics and precision medicine, machine learning models are often "black boxes," predicting phenotypes from genotypes without understanding the mechanisms by which such translation occurs. This project addresses that deficiency by creating a library of large-scale maps of cellular structure and function across demographic and disease contexts.

Much of cell structure remains uncharted, and cell mapping technologies have typically been applied separately; integration of multiple complementary data modalities provides the opportunity to incorporate biological structure robustly across physical scales.

Construction of hierarchical cell maps: directed acyclic graphs in which each node represents an assembly of proteins in proximity at a given scale, spanning from large assemblies representing cell compartments to small assemblies of proteins in close proximity.
Self-supervised multimodal embedding of protein-protein interaction and immunofluorescence image features into a shared low-dimensional space.
Multi-resolution community detection over protein-protein similarities to generate a hierarchy of protein assemblies.
Development of visible machine learning models (visible neural networks) that interrogate how protein assemblies in the cell affect cell-level phenotype predictions.
Interpretation of genetic variants and mutations in human genomics using cell maps as a structural prior.

Production Location recorded for the release: University of California San Diego; University of California San Francisco; Stanford University; University of Virginia.

Data were generated from commercially available, ethically sourced human cell lines rather than collected directly from individuals. The MDA-MB-468 cell line is available from ATCC; the KOLF2.1J iPSC line was derived from a healthy male Northern European donor and is available from the Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Initiative (HipSci) resource.
Data in this release was derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large.

Targeted selection of cell lines and perturbation targets. CM4AI's objective is multimodal interrogation of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders in disease-relevant cell lines under perturbed and unperturbed conditions.

MDA-MB-468 triple negative breast cancer cells (with and without paclitaxel or vorinostat) and KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells (with and without differentiation into neural progenitor cells, neurons, and cardiomyocytes).
Downloaded PPI networks are processed using the node2vec deep learning model to reduce dimensionality, producing a PPI embedding that contains information about the protein's interactions.
IF images are processed using a Human Protein Atlas deep learning model to reduce dimensionality, producing an image embedding that contains information about protein localization.

The PPI and image embeddings are integrated to obtain a co-embedding for each protein using contrastive deep learning. This integration model learns co-embeddings such that the original embeddings can be reconstructed with minimal information loss and proteins with similar PPI and image embeddings have similar co-embeddings.
Community detection is performed based on the all-by-all similarities of pairs of proteins in the co-embedding space; the resulting hierarchy of protein communities is output as the final cell map.

Cell maps are annotated in a two-pronged approach. First, cell maps are aligned to known protein function and pathway resources, including the Gene Ontology (GO) and Reactome, to determine protein assemblies in the cell map with high overlap with known cell biology. Second, assemblies in the cell maps are annotated using a large language model approach developed by the project to name sets of proteins and assign a name confidence score.
DenseNet / Human Protein Atlas image classification model

node2vec is used to represent each protein as a feature vector based on its protein-protein interaction neighborhood. A Human Protein Atlas deep learning model is used to reduce the dimensionality of immunofluorescence images into an image embedding. A large language model approach developed by the project names sets of proteins and assigns a name confidence score.
Perturb-seq data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (with and without treatment)
SEC-MS data in KOLF2.1J iPSCs (undifferentiated, NPC, neuron, and cardiomyocyte)
SEC-MS data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (with and without treatment)
AP-MS data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (treated with paclitaxel)
AP-MS data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (treated with vorinostat)

All ten files in the release are distributed as ZIP archives via the University of Virginia Dataverse. The Dataverse page notes that files above the 1.9 GB download limit cannot be downloaded as a ZIP through the browser and directs users to the Data Access API for programmatic access.

Published 2026-06-17 (Version 2.0). The AP-MS, mass-spec, perturb-seq, and release metadata files are recorded as Published Jun 17, 2026; the three immunofluorescence image archives are recorded as Published Jul 15, 2026.

Component data are additionally deposited in external repositories: SEC-MS and AP-MS mass spectrometry data at the MassIVE Repository, and the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas of iPSCs at Figshare. Perturb-seq data in KOLF2.1J iPSCs and in MDA-MB-468 cells are listed as Embargoed.

Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - Data Release, cited in the CM4AI preprint as available in LibraData, the University of Virginia's archival data repository, V1.

Clark T, Mohan J, Schaffer L, Obernier K, et al. Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence: AI-Ready Maps of Human Cell Architecture from Disease-Relevant Cell Lines. bioRxiv preprint, posted May 24, 2024. Recorded as the Related Publication for the release.
Nourreddine S, Doctor Y, Dailamy A, et al. A perturbation cell atlas of human induced pluripotent stem cells. bioRxiv. 2024 Nov 4; PMCID PMC11580897. Listed as a Related Publication for the release.

That work acknowledges Bridge2AI Program funding OT2 OD032742.
Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence data releases

The CM4AI quarterly data release series, of which this release is one instance. CM4AI delivers machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data, together with quarterly data releases of map-input data streams.

The CM4AI web portal maintains a Publications page for work arising from the project, and a Data Releases page listing the current release alongside an archive of the May 2024, March 2025, June 2025, and October 2025 releases.

CM4AI consists of three pillars - Data, People, and Ethics - organized into six modules: Data Acquisition, Tools, and Standards (Data); Skills and Workforce Development, and Teaming (People); and Ethics. The Standards Module packages data, software, metadata and provenance graphs using the FAIRSCAPE framework, which creates RO-Crate packages and assigns persistent, resolvable, globally unique identifiers using the ARK scheme, with provenance entailments expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology. CM4AI defines AI-Ready biomedical data as fully characterized FAIR data of known provenance that can be ethically and reliably processed by AI applications, whose models and software are available and well-described for validation and re-use, and whose predictions may be fully explained and interpreted to the user as needed; the project's stated criteria are FAIR, Provenanced, Characterized, Explainable, and Ethical.
